machine.name: Apple M5 Pro
machine.reference: official BLAKE3 1.8.7: b3sum and the blake3 crate with NEON + rayon

status_note: Interim numbers; HF model and outboard results are added as they land.

in_memory.note: Warm, data already in memory, same bytes and same digest. Rust = blake3 crate (NEON + rayon).

cli.note: One-shot `b3sum FILE...` (process start included), medians of 15 interleaved rounds; output byte-identical to the official b3sum.

daemon.note: Long-running process, start-up excluded: every round re-opens, re-maps and re-hashes the files. Rust seq = one file at a time like b3sum; Rust par = rayon across files (strongest baseline).

iroh.note: iroh-blobs 0.103 ingest (add_path: BLAKE3 hash + bao outboard) into a fresh store vs Bend. Bend outboard support in progress; these Bend numbers are root hash only.

floors: Page faults on a mapped file: ~15 ms per GiB, serialized in the kernel (shared by every tool).
All-core CPU ceiling near 38 GB/s for BLAKE3 on this chip (Rust and Bend both reach it).
macOS open(): ~48 ms per 10,000 files at best, however many threads (volume-wide serialization).
GPU start-up: the Metal heap costs ~50 ms per GiB to set up, so one-shot CLI runs stay on the CPU.

techniques.title: BLAKE3 core in Bend2
techniques.summary: Unboxed U32 records compile to register code; Array<U32> is a packed buffer; Array.fork shares input down a parallel fork tree.

techniques.title: 8-lane compress8 + clang SLP
techniques.summary: Eight chunks per call, word-major lanes, one call site, SLP and inline flags: 2.95 GB/s per core vs NEON's 2.40.

techniques.title: b3sum I/O path
techniques.summary: Parallel one-pass loader, zero-copy read-only mmap, byte-balanced file tree, one write for all output.

techniques.title: Files past 4 GiB
techniques.summary: 1 GiB segments are complete BLAKE3 subtrees, hashed in parallel and merged as parents; up to 4 TiB.

techniques.title: Flat GPU leaves
techniques.summary: Fork-free 4/16/64-chunk leaves sized to the 16,384-lane cube: 93-110 GB/s on the GPU.
